## Summary

Universal Electronics (UEI) is an American smart-home technology provider founded in 1986, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona with R&D in Santa Ana, California, and listed on Nasdaq as UEIC; it holds an estimated 30 percent global share of home-entertainment remotes and makes products for audio-video, subscription-broadcasting, connected-home, tablet and smartphone companies [2]. The IEEE registry lists 29 MA-L blocks under "Universal Electronics, Inc.", 28 at the Santa Ana address and one at a Cypress, California address [1]; a separate "Universal Electronics BV" block is registered in Enschede, where UEI has a regional office, but is not aliased here because it is a distinct registrant name [1][2].

A MAC in a UEI block is most likely a remote control, a thermostat or a home-security sensor shipped under another brand or under One For All, Ecolink, Nevo or UEI TIDE [2][3]. UEI's own site lists infrared, Bluetooth, Zigbee, Z-Wave and sub-GHz connectivity across its control products, thermostats and wireless security sensors [3]. No security advisory or NVD record naming Universal Electronics was found; silicon and FCC grantee codes are not listed because the FCC ID databases refused automated access from the session that wrote this entry, and randomization is unknown.
